Run every workflow of a workflow set through one nested design

Source: R/nested-workflow-map.R
nested_workflow_map.Rd

nested_workflow_map() runs every workflow of a workflowsets::workflow_set() through one nested design, so you can compare models on the same outer folds.

Usage

nested_workflow_map(object, fn = "nested_tune_grid", ...)

Arguments

object

A workflow set.

fn

The name of the function to run each workflow through. The default is "nested_tune_grid". The others are "nested_tune_bayes", "nested_tune_race_anova", "nested_tune_race_win_loss" and "nested_tune_sim_anneal". With "nested_fit_resamples", no workflow can have a parameter to tune.

...

The arguments of fn, each one named. resamples, the nested design, is required, and a control goes here as well. A name that fn does not take is an error. A metrics set reaches every workflow, and one that does not suit a workflow's model is an error before any workflow runs. Under every selection_rule() but "desirability", its first metric chooses each fold's candidate.

Value

A nested_results_set, a tibble with one row per workflow. Its columns are wflow_id, workflow, and result, the workflow's nested_results. It is not a workflow_set, so workflowsets::rank_results() and tune::fit_best() do not accept it. Choosing the best workflow by its nested estimate is a selection that the outer loop did not nest.

Details

The function works like workflowsets::workflow_map(). fn names the nested function to run, and its arguments come through .... Unlike in workflowsets, an entry in the set's option column overrides an argument of the same name in ..., for that workflow alone. The workflows run in the set's order, and the set's own result column is not read.

A workflow with no tune::tune() marker runs through nested_fit_resamples(), whatever fn names, so a baseline can sit beside the tuned models. Each workflow gets only the arguments its function takes. So a grid reaches the tuned workflows and not the fixed one, and the fixed one runs under tune's default control unless its option entry names one.

There is no seed argument, so call set.seed() first. Each workflow starts from the same random state, so fold i of every workflow runs under the same two seeds. Each result is identical to a call by hand on that workflow, with the same arguments, after the same set.seed().

An error from one workflow names that workflow at the front of its message and keeps its class. So does a warning about failed folds. An error stops the call, so nothing is returned, even for the workflows that already ran.

collect_metrics() and the other collect_*() functions stack each workflow's table under a wflow_id column. nested_final_fit() with an id fits one workflow.

dplyr::filter(), dplyr::arrange(), dplyr::mutate() and x[i, ] keep the class. They keep it only while the wflow_id, workflow and result columns keep their values. An operation that empties the set, repeats a wflow_id, changes or drops one of those columns, or brings in a row from elsewhere returns a plain tibble. So does a direct vctrs::vec_cbind(). dplyr::group_by(), dplyr::rowwise() and tibble::as_tibble() return other classes that still carry the fn attribute. A value replaced with $<- or [[<- is not checked.

See also

nested_tune_grid(), nested_fit_resamples(), collect_metrics.nested_results_set(), nested_final_fit(), workflowsets::workflow_map()

Examples

data(mtcars)

rec <- recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars) |>
  recipes::step_pca(recipes::all_predictors(), num_comp = tune::tune())
wf <- workflows::workflow(rec, parsnip::linear_reg())

set.seed(1)
folds <- nested_resamples(
  mtcars,
  outside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2),
  inside = rsample::vfold_cv(v = 2)
)
# One tuned workflow and one baseline, on the same nested design.
wset <- workflowsets::workflow_set(
  preproc = list(pca = rec, none = recipes::recipe(mpg ~ ., data = mtcars)),
  models = list(lm = parsnip::linear_reg())
)

set.seed(2)
res <- nested_workflow_map(wset, resamples = folds, grid = data.frame(num_comp = 1:2))
res
#> 
#> ── Nested cross-validation results for a workflow set ─────────────────
#> Orchestrator: `nested_tune_grid()` (grid search)
#> Workflows: 2
#> ✔ "pca_lm": 2 of 2 outer folds completed (grid search)
#> ✔ "none_lm": 2 of 2 outer folds completed (no tuning)
#> ℹ Use `collect_metrics()` for every workflow's estimate under its id,
#>   and `x$result[[i]]` for one workflow's run.
collect_metrics(res)
#> # A tibble: 4 × 6
#>   wflow_id .metric .estimator  mean     n std_err
#>   <chr>    <chr>   <chr>      <dbl> <int>   <dbl>
#> 1 pca_lm   rmse    standard   2.98      2  0.459 
#> 2 pca_lm   rsq     standard   0.747     2  0.0691
#> 3 none_lm  rmse    standard   5.93      2  2.06  
#> 4 none_lm  rsq     standard   0.495     2  0.119 

# The baseline ran through nested_fit_resamples(), whatever fn named.
extract_procedure(res$result[[2]])$tuner
#> [1] "fit_resamples"
